Package com.openvireo.core.hosts

Class JavaNetHttpTransport

java.lang.Object
com.openvireo.core.hosts.JavaNetHttpTransport
All Implemented Interfaces:
HttpTransport
public final class JavaNetHttpTransport extends Object implements HttpTransport
The default
invalid reference 
HttpTransport
on the JVM: java.net.http.HttpClient (JDK 11+), fully asynchronous.

As ov_core::host::HttpTransport requires: - No redirects: the client is built with Redirect.NEVER, so a 3xx comes back as a response and the core refuses it. A client passed in must be built the same way. - No cookies: the client has no CookieHandler (a client passed in with one is refused). - Any status is a response: 4xx/5xx come back with their body, never as an exception. - Headers: the request's headers, in order, plus what the platform always adds (User-Agent, Host, Content-Length). The headers java.net.http reserves for itself (Connection, Content-Length, Expect, Host, Upgrade) are left to it. Header values may be bearer tokens and are never logged. - Errors: no network, DNS failure or connection refused → TransportException.Offline, a timeout → Timeout, TLS → Tls, anything else → Other. - Streams (openStream, server-sent events): the response comes back when its headers arrive, and nextChunk hands over each piece of the body as it is received.

requestTimeout bounds the wait for a response's headers (null waits forever).
